brief.headline: Renato has lost 8.3% of his body weight (84.1 to 77.1 kg, Sep 5 to Nov 24) and now needs moderate help with bathing and lower-body dressing. He was also hospitalized Oct 27 for chest pain.

items.statement: Weight fell from 84.1 kg on Sep 5 to 77.1 kg on Nov 24, 2026 (-7.0 kg, -8.3%). Readings were 81.7 kg on Oct 1 and 79.2 kg on Oct 28. On Nov 24 the dietitian noted poor appetite, skipped breakfasts, and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. Plan: oral nutrition supplement twice daily, weekly weights, and a dental check for chewing problems.
items.verifier_note: Weights, change (-7.0 kg, -8.3%), and dietitian findings and plan all match the vitals record and the Nov 24 note.

items.statement: On Sep 30, OT reassessment found moderate assistance now needed for bathing and lower-body dressing. He was independent at the last review. On Sep 24 the aide gave hands-on help out of the tub, and he said he has been skipping showers because he fears slipping. OT recommends a tub transfer bench, handheld shower, and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: The Sep 24 aide note and Sep 30 OT note support every detail, including the recommendations and the prior independence.

items.statement: He was seen in the partner hospital ED on Oct 27, 2026 for chest pain and admitted for 3 days. The cardiac workup was negative and no new medications were started. At the Nov 3 PCP follow-up he was back to baseline per his spouse, and the PCP planned close monitoring for two weeks.
items.verifier_note: The ED visit on Oct 27, the 3-day admission, the negative workup, and no new medications are in the discharge summary. The Nov 3 note supports baseline per spouse and two weeks of close monitoring.

items.statement: The Sep 24 note records fear of slipping in the tub, with avoidance of showers. This raises a fall-risk and hygiene concern while the bathing equipment and added support are not yet confirmed in place.
items.verifier_note: The fear of slipping and shower avoidance are documented. The notes show only that equipment and hours were recommended. They don't say whether the equipment was confirmed in place, so 'not yet confirmed' is an inference from absence. 'Hygiene concern' is also interpretive.

items.statement: The record shows no medication starts or stops since Sep 1. The weight loss and appetite change are not yet linked to any medication change in the evidence.
items.verifier_note: The medications record shows no starts or stops since Sep 1. The dietitian note doesn't link the weight loss or appetite change to any medication.

questions_for_team: Who will confirm that the tub transfer bench, handheld shower, and added bathing hours are in place, and by when?
Are the weekly weights and twice-daily supplements under way? What weight or intake change would prompt escalation?
Could the weight loss and the chest pain admission be related, and does the PCP want further review beyond the planned 2-week monitoring?
Has the dental check for chewing problems been scheduled?
Does the decline in bathing and dressing, along with the weight loss, call for a cognition or care-needs reassessment, given his Alzheimer's diagnosis?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters, ED visits, and admissions in that window; note any since the last IDT review.
Falls and near-falls review: count, circumstances, injuries, and whether fall-risk screening was repeated, given osteoporosis, chronic low back pain, and fibromyalgia.

Medication reconciliation: the chart lists alteplase (100 MG injection, start 2022-02-04), clopidogrel, and galantamine (start 2025-11-02). Verify the alteplase entry is a valid active order (it is unusual as a chronic outpatient medication), confirm clopidogrel indication and bleeding-risk review, and check for any starts or stops in the window.

Galantamine follow-up after Alzheimer's onset (2025-11-02): check titration status, GI side effects, weight, appetite, and whether cholinesterase-inhibitor tolerance has been reviewed by the prescriber.
Cognition and behavior: review any cognitive screen scores, new confusion, agitation, wandering, or safety concerns since the diagnosis; confirm the care plan addresses them.
Weight and BMI trend across the window (obesity, prediabetes, hyperlipidemia), plus any nutrition or dietary-intake concerns.
Glycemic and lipid monitoring: check whether HbA1c/fasting glucose and lipid panel are due or resulted in the window, given prediabetes and hyperlipidemia.
Anemia follow-up: review most recent hemoglobin/CBC, iron studies if done, and any bleeding signs, especially while on clopidogrel.
Respiratory status for emphysema: check oxygen use, inhaler use, dyspnea scores, exacerbations, and vaccination status.

Pain and function: review pain scores, analgesic use (including any opioid or NSAID changes), ADL/IADL performance, mobility aids, and mood/sleep for chronic pain and fibromyalgia; confirm allergy list (lisinopril, peanut) is current and any reactions are documented.
